title: Resilient SLA fallback proxy and utilization folding
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Add a resilient SLA fallback proxy to route excess load to compatible model variants and a utilization-folding telemetry component to produce stable utilization signals for Dedicated autoscaling. Includes instrumentation and rollout docs.
description:
Context: In high-tail traffic or during partial capacity loss we observed short-lived SLA breaches driven by microbursts and noisy utilization signals. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a lightweight SLA Fallback Proxy that sits in the Dedicated request path and performs fast, policy-driven reroutes to compatible model variants or secondary capacity tiers when latency risk is detected; (2) a Utilization Folding component that aggregates high-frequency utilization into a folded, hysteresis-aware signal used by the autoscaler to avoid reactive oscillation.

Motivation: Existing autoscaler reacts to raw utilization spikes and microbursts which causes scale thrash and unnecessary warmup traffic. The Fallback Proxy reduces user-visible SLA violations by routing critical requests to safer backends while Utilization Folding stabilizes the scale decision input stream. Together they reduce tail latency and unnecessary provisioning.

- Initial implementation of fallback proxy and policy engine (src/autoscaler/fallback_proxy.go, internal/autoscaler/policy.go) -- 2026-02-18

- E2E tests for fallback behavior under partial cluster failure and microburst (e2e/dedicated/fallback_e2e_test.go) -- 2026-02-24

Files changed (high level):
- src/autoscaler/fallback_proxy.go: new component that intercepts request routing; implements fast path decision and metrics emission.
- internal/autoscaler/policy.go: policy DSL and parser for fallback rules (tenant-level overrides supported).
- pkg/telemetry/folding.go: folding algorithm (exponential folding + percentile-weighted smoothing) and config surface.
- cmd/dedicated-agent/main.go: hooks into agent startup to register folding consumer.
- metrics/registry.go: new metric families: dedicated_util_folded, dedicated_fallback_reroutes_total, dedicated_fallback_reasons.
- e2e/dedicated/fallback_e2e_test.go: integration scenarios with partial pool drain and microburst replay.
- docs/*: rollout guidance and examples.
- charts/*: opt-in flag and default off in values.yaml.

Design notes (short):
- Fallback proxy is intentionally cheap: it only evaluates a small set of signals (sequence length, model compatibility table, current per-tenant latency SLO risk) and must return within 250µs on the hot path. When a fallback occurs we emit a reroute metric and a structured event for traceability.
- Utilization folding: the approach blends a short-term exponential fold (alpha) with a percentile-based lift to retain signal about sustained high tails without being dominated by single-sample spikes. Tunable knobs: fold_alpha, percentile_window_seconds, hysteresis_ratio.
- Autoscaler integration: autoscaler now consumes dedicated_util_folded rather than raw utilization. A transitional mode (two-cycle compare) is implemented so rollout won't flip heuristics instantly.

Review convo (abridged, continuous):
Maya Chen: "Nice separation of concerns. A couple of questions: 1) how do we prevent fallback amplification when multiple tenants fallback concurrently? 2) can you add a metric that tags fallback by model-variant?"
Ethan Park: "For 1) the policy includes a soft quota per-pool to avoid amplification; I added a candidate backpressure flag (fallback_backpressure_enabled) that toggles spillover. For 2) added dedicated_fallback_variant label on the reroute metric. Tests included."
Luca Moretti: "folding.go looks good, but the percentile window default is long for small tenants—can we make it tenant-aware?"
Ethan Park: "Good call. Exposed percentile_window_seconds and added tenant_weighted_defaults in policy. Doc updated to recommend smaller windows for bursty tenants."
Riley Gomez: "CI flake on e2e timed out once, reran and passed. Approving pending minor log level tweak."
Ethan Park: "Adjusted log levels and dropped a noisy debug. Ready to merge."

CI summary: 
- unit (go test): pass
- e2e: initially one timeout on fallback_e2e_test.go, rerun passed
- lint: pass
- security-scan: pass (no new deps)
- performance-smoke: baseline within 5% of main in our bench harness

Rollout plan: 
1) Merge to main behind helm opt-in (default off).
2) Enable for internal dogfood cluster with 1% of tenants; monitor dedicated_util_folded and fallback_reroutes_total for anomalies.
3) If stable after 48h, enable tenant opt-in via tenant policy.
4) Gradually flip default for new clusters after one week of stability.

Metrics/observability to watch: dedicated_util_folded (p50/p90/p99), dedicated_fallback_reroutes_total (by reason), dedicated_fallback_latency_histogram, autoscaler_decisions (pre/post fold).

Known limitations and TODOs: 
- We currently rely on the model compatibility table for fallback decisions; automated compatibility analysis will be added in a follow-up (ENG-4786).
- Fallback proxy does not yet support tiered pricing signals — follow-up will add billing tags.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals from Maya, Luca, and Riley. No migrations required. Feature remains off by default.

If you want to run locally: see docs/dedicated/fallback.md for dev harness steps and e2e replay instructions.
notes: Opt-in feature; designed to reduce SLA surface area during transient congestion and produce stable scaling metrics. Verified in performance harness and dogfood cluster before merge.
